sections.title: Executive Summary
paragraphs: The aim of this document is to describe the JICustomField web service in terms of "what is it" and "how to use it". It describes the webservice data-model, supported operation and related behavior and available interfaces.
Before going deeper with specific features of this webservice please ensure to review the document “JINT WS Development_Kit - Web Services Overview” which applies to all webservices
The structure of the current document is the following:

2. Request data format: describes the structure of the import request. The request is composed of sections and every section is composed of fields to be filled. This paragraph specifies which fields are mandatory and those that can be omitted.
3. Behavior: describes how the web service processes the data passed in input, in case of some processes.
4. Response data format: describes the structure of the web service response and contains the list of possible error codes.
6. Available methods: contains the list of the methods provided by the web service.
7. WSDL: in this paragraph is attached the JICustomField.wsdl from which the web service has been created and is to be used to generate the client.
8. Endpoints: available webservice SOAP endpoint URLs
9. Request samples: sample SOAP requests to invoke the webservice
11. Operation and Endpoints: describes REST available collections. Allowed calls with allowed parameters and supported HTTP methods
12. Request Samples: provides some call examples and a POSTMAN collection with an extensive list of runnable calls

13. Data Types and UI Default Labels: describes the type of the fields and the corresponding label in English language in the platform with the aim to simplify the mapping between the fields visible in the platform and the fields used in the web service

sections.title: Custom Field import method
paragraphs: The Custom Field Import method enables importing custom fields from the customer ERP to the Jaggaer Indirect platform.

sections.title: Request data format
paragraphs: Following table shows the structure of the import request to submit. For each entity are marked in bold the key attributes used by the insert/update policy implemented by the service.

rows:
Container of one or more CustomField data defining custom field data to be imported.
See section CustomField [Custom Field Import method].

Container of one or more Relationship data defining relationship to be imported.
See section Relationship [Custom Field Import method]
Indicates whether the custom field should (1) or should not (0) be active within the Jaggaer indirect solution.
Description of the custom field to be displayed externally (for example, on a PO)

Indicates whether the custom field can (1) or cannot (0) be subject to splits within a PR. Splitting a custom field allows the user to assign various distributions across multiple values for the custom field. This field is only valid for custom fields within the Codes section of the PR.
Indicates whether the custom field can (1) or cannot (0) be shown on plain text email PO revisions sent to the supplier.

Method to be used when sorting custom field values in search results and the user's profile.
Allowed values are:
Alpha-numeric - The values are sorted alpha-numerically.
Explicitly - The values are sorted in the order specified on the Administration > organization setup > Custom Fields > Values tab.

Indicates whether the custom field is (1) or is not (0) to be added to the MBU Chart-of-Accounts list. When this field is set to 1, you can uniquely assign the custom field to a specific business unit in your organization.
Note: Setting this field to 0 for a parent custom field also sets it to false for all its children.

Indicates whether values associated with the custom field can (1) or cannot (0) be part of dynamic workflow. JAGGAER Services must set up the associated dynamic workflow step or activity before you can set this field to true.

Style to be applied to the custom field.
Possible values:
0 - Use user profile permissions -This style uses the custom field permissions as set up in the user's profile or role.
1 - Yes/No (checkbox) - This style shows up as a checkbox in the JAGGAER Indirect solution UI for the user to select. The user must have either the View or Edit Personal List custom field permission to be able to see and select the checkbox. Default values saved in the profile are not automatically applied.
2 - Organization-wide list - This style shows the user all your organization's values within the Values tab in a drop-down list on the PR or PO.
Help text that is to appear when the user selects the custom field name in the JAGGAER Indirect solution UI
Indicates whether automatic approval is (1) or is not (0) enabled by default for any new rule created, if the individual placing the order is an approver of the rule.

Container of one or more CustomFieldValue data defining customFieldValue to be imported.
See section CustomFieldValue [Custom Field Import method].

Action to perform on the custom field value.
Allowed values:
modify - Update the existing value or add a value if none exists.
delete - Delete the value, provided a relationship does not exist.
If a relationship does exist for the value, you must delete the relationship before you can delete the value.
Description of the custom field value.

Indicates whether the value should (1) or should not (0) be active for shoppers in the JAGGAER Indirect solution.
An active item is available to appropriate end users when shopping in the solution. An inactive item is not available to end users. A value might be marked inactive even if it has relationships in place.

sections.title: Custom Field identification strategy
paragraphs: System uses value provided in “name” field of CustomField [Error! Reference source not found.] structure to identify the custom field within Jaggaer Indirect platform.

sections.title: Response data format
paragraphs: Custom Fields response is made of following fields:

rows:
Global Operation result.
This code is about the web service call, not about import result.
For information about import, consider data specified in responseMessage field.
See Error codes below for a list of possible global code
Global result description. If operation completed successfully, it is “OK”, otherwise it is a brief explanation of mismatches found.

Import operation result description inserted if provided data is formally correct and no generic error (e.g.: communication error) was found.
If a problem occurred during the import, the responseMessage includes appropriate warning or error messages
See section ResponseMessage [Custom Field Import method]

Effective import result description.
See section Status [Custom Field Import method]

Container of errors generated during importing of custom fields or relationship between custom fields.
See section ObjectErrors [Custom Field Import method]

Import response result code.
200 - The request was processed successfully in its entirety with no warnings or errors.
201 - The custom field was imported successfully, but one or more warnings were generated. The warnings are included in the response.
Any other code indicates an import failure. For instance:
403 - Custom field import failed because the customer is not configured for integration traffic on Jaggaer Indirect platform.
406 - The request could not be understood due to syntax errors.
500 - The request could not be processed due to a transient error.

List of the common HTTP failure errors that might be generated during a custom field import.
See section Error [Custom Field Import method]

Container of CustomFieldRef.
See section CustomFieldRef [Custom Field Import method]

Container of RelationshipRef.
See section RelationshipRef [Custom Field Import method]

Zero or more CustomFieldValueSetRef.
See section CustomFieldValueSetRef [Custom Field Import method]

Zero or more Error data generated during import of custom field
See section Error [Custom Field Import method]

Zero or more CustomFieldValueRef data
See section CustomFieldValueRef [Custom Field Import method]

List of Error data
See section Error [Custom Field Import method]
Custom field name of the child custom field.
Custom field name of the parent custom field.

One or more Error data.
See section Error [Custom Field Import method]

One or more ParentCustomFieldValueRef data
See section ParentCustomFieldValueRef [Error! Reference source not found.]

Indicates whether the problem that occurred is an error, a warning, or informational.
Allowed values are:
Error
Warning
Info
Text of the error, warning, or informational message

sections.title: Error codes
paragraphs: The web service call returns a code defining the result of the operation:

rows:
Provided data was successfully received and used to try creating objects.
That means that data is formally correct, but to know if operation really successes or failed it is necessary to analyse other response part.
Operation was not completed due to error in provided data.
Invalid SOAP Request Object (SOAP Request doesn’t match web service definition or request contains information that are not compliant with instance configuration or user permission)
Unauthorized Method (Web Service method isn’t configured to be executed)
Unable to acquire lock (Web Service is configured to serialize different call coming from a same client and it hasn’t been able to acquire lock to satisfy request for configured timeout)

sections.title: WSDL
paragraphs: in the following WSDL file the URLs of the service end-points are invalid. The real URLs will be provided after the activation of the JINT component.

Once the integration set-up is completed, an updated version of WSDL files will be made available within the following URL (where MY-SERVER will be substituted with the URL of JINT module for the given customer, communicated immediately after the activation).

‘Live’ WSDL file can change without notice to include new fields but is guaranteed backward compatibility regarding message exchanges (i.e. new fields will be available only to newly activated integrations).
For this reason, the WS client component should always refer to the WSDL file provided at the time the JINT is activated.
